vBRIEFInfo.description: README, deployment guide, and supplementary docs

narrative.Overview: Write the user-facing documentation: README.md (5-minute deploy guide, quickstart, mode selection), and supplementary docs for high-volume setups, China VPS hosting, and scaling. Documentation is the last scope — written after all services are implemented so instructions are accurate. Depends on: proxy-mode-stack, test-suite.
narrative.Traces: NFR-1 (<5 min deploy — README is the guide), NFR-2 (China/high-volume — documented in docs/)

items.title: README.md — 5-minute deploy guide
items.description: Write README.md covering: project description + badges (CI, license), prerequisites (Docker + Docker Compose), quickstart (4 steps: clone, cp .env.example .env + edit, docker compose up, point DNS), mode selection table (standalone vs proxy, what each starts), first-run behaviour (admin auto-created, token auto-generated), SSH access instructions, and a Troubleshooting section (common errors: Let's Encrypt rate limits, port 80 blocked, Forgejo not starting).

items.title: docs/high-volume.md
items.description: Document high-volume configuration: recommended GH_PROXY_CACHE_SIZE values by disk size, tuning GH_PROXY_RATE_LIMIT_RPS, reading Prometheus metrics at :9090/metrics, connecting Prometheus + Grafana, and signs that ghproxy is the bottleneck vs Forgejo vs network.

items.title: docs/china-hosting.md
items.description: Document China-first deployment: recommended VPS providers (DMIT HK/LA CN2 GIA, BandwagonHost LA CN2 GIA), recommended specs (1Gbps+, 8+ cores, 16GB RAM, NVMe), network topology explanation (CN2 GIA vs BGP), DNS setup for low-latency resolution, and verifying latency from mainland China.

items.title: docs/scaling.md
items.description: Document scaling beyond a single VPS: running ghproxy on a separate node with Caddy load balancing, adding a read replica Forgejo, backup strategy (forgejo_data volume snapshot), and upgrade procedure (pull new images, docker compose up -d, verify health).

items.title: License file
items.description: Add LICENSE file. Choose an appropriate open-source license (MIT recommended for maximum adoption as per project goal of being a reusable open-source project). Confirm choice with project owner before committing.
